title: Interview: grocery items, categories, staples and units
lead: Define the canonical item vocabulary: categories, initial staples, and unit handling.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Item matching, list ordering and later the pantry estimates all depend on categories and units. The category order should match how the household's store app or store is laid out, to make ordering quick (L4).

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. Category list and order (e.g., produce, meat, dairy, bakery, canned, dry goods, spices, frozen, household, pet). Should it match the primary store app's departments?
2. Initial staples list (always-buy or frequently-low items, including pet items).
3. Unit conversions: convert within a dimension (tsp↔tbsp↔cup, oz↔lb) (recommended), or never convert?
4. Should pantry spices and basics (salt, pepper, oil) ever appear on the list automatically? (recommend: no, unless marked as a staple that's low)
5. How to treat "1 can (15 oz)": count of cans (recommended) or weight?

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `local/` private notes (not committed)
- `docs/decisions/0019-items-categories-units.md` (new)
- `src/larder/data/seed_items.toml` (seed data, written in the parser/matching slices)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Ask the questions, showing all ingredient lines from the imported recipes as concrete examples.
2. Write ADR 0019 and record the raw answers in `local/` (not committed).
3. Update the ingredient parser, matching and list slices (`slicer edit`).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- ADR 0019 has the category order, staples and unit policy.
- Dependent slices are updated.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
